title: Level-one weight at extremal noise stability
statement: Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Choose $x$ uniformly from the sign cube and, independently in each coordinate, obtain $y$ by keeping $x_i$ with probability $1/3$ and replacing it by $-x_i$ with probability $2/3$. If $\mathbb E[f(x)f(y)]=-1/3$, then the level-one Fourier weight of $f$, the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients over singleton coordinate sets, is $1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
The noise stability at correlation $-1/3$ equals $-1/3$
